scope: evidence-based visual cues in Finnish YKI prep app
score_policy: evidenceFit100 are editorial relevance/confidence ratings (0-100), NOT measured teaching efficacy
effects_warning: Standardized g/r/d estimates concern signaling and broad emotional design, NOT color alone or guaranteed Finnish/YKI gains New 2026 subgroup combined cue effect CI overlaps zero; visual types pooled, and 2008 L2 enhancement can compete with meaning processing.

sources.title: A meta-analysis of how signaling affects learning with media
sources.finding: Signaling mechanisms, including but not limited to colors, support retention g=0.53 and transfer g=0.33; no evidence these sizes belong to color alone.

sources.title: Signaling text-picture relations in multimedia learning: A comprehensive meta-analysis
sources.finding: Positive signaled multimedia comprehension/transfer r=0.17; stronger for lower prior knowledge.

sources.title: A meta-analysis of signaling principle in multimedia learning environments
sources.finding: Overall signaling-associated learning outcome d=0.38; may overlap with other meta-analyses; cannot add effects.

sources.title: Investigating textual enhancement and captions in L2 grammar and vocabulary
sources.finding: Caption benefits robust for L2 Spanish target vocab but selective for grammar structures.

sources.title: The Effects of Textually Enhanced Captions on Written Elicited Imitation in L2 Grammar
sources.finding: Whole-form or inflection-specific text enhancement improved some Spanish grammar performance; n=28, transfer to Finnish unverified.

sources.title: The contributions of color to recognition memory for natural scenes
sources.finding: Recognition of natural colored scenes 5–10% better than black-and-white; not generalizable to grammar recall.

sources.title: The influence of content-relevant background color as a retrieval cue on learning with multimedia
sources.finding: Background color alone not sufficient retrieval cue; ceiling/floor caveats.

sources.title: Meta-Analysis of Emotional Designs in Multimedia Learning: A Replication and Extension Study
sources.finding: Emotional design may improve learning; not isolated to individual hues; color alone literature more limited.

sources.title: How effective is emotional design? A meta-analysis on facial anthropomorphisms and pleasant colors during multimedia learning
sources.finding: Pleasant colors and/or anthropomorphic cues jointly associated with retention d=0.387; not isolated color effect.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
sources.finding: Simple highlighting low utility; practice testing and spaced practice high utility.

sources.title: Color Psychology: Effects of Perceiving Color on Psychological Functioning in Humans
sources.finding: Context-dependent cognitive and emotional associations; caution over general claims.

sources.authors: Limited evidence for the effect of red color on cognitive performance
sources.title: Limited evidence for the effect of red color on cognitive performance: A meta-analysis
sources.finding: No convincing effect for anagrams or knowledge tasks; reasoning effects smaller and mostly from earlier studies.

sources.title: Does task-irrelevant colour information create extraneous cognitive load?
sources.finding: Task-irrelevant conflicting colors can interfere with some associative learning tasks; avoid misleading hue.

sources.title: The Influence of Colour on Memory Performance: A Review
sources.finding: Possible color–attention–memory relations, not a universal best hue.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2
sources.finding: Don't encode status by color alone; text 4.5:1, large text/UI 3:1.

sources.title: Effects of cueing interventions on online learning outcomes: a meta-analytic review of 40 studies
sources.finding: Overall cueing g=0.320; visual group g=0.261 [0.078,0.444] blends colors, captions, bold, highlights; negative combined cue estimate confidence interval overlaps zero. Subgroup comparison not causal head-to-head.
sources.scope: online teaching mainly videos, mixed cues; not exact hue or Finnish YKI effect

sources.title: Visual Input Enhancement and Grammar Learning: A Meta-Analytic Review
sources.finding: In 16 L2 primary studies (20 samples) visual text enhancement d=+0.22 grammar learning but d=-0.26 meaning processing. Distinguish form noticing from reading comprehension.
sources.scope: foreign language input enhancement; not Finnish, highlights may include bold/typographic cues

sources.title: An eye-tracking study of how color coding affects multimedia learning
sources.finding: With text-image correspondence, color coding reduced search effort and improved retention/transfer for this multimedia task; not universal color-memory rule.
sources.scope: paired text and illustration educational material

sources.title: Retrieval practice produces more learning than elaborative studying with concept mapping
sources.finding: Active retrieval aids meaningful long-term learning vs elaborative re-study, supporting no-cue delayed transfer after visual explanation.
sources.scope: retrieval practice educational text; does not compare colors

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 1.4.1 Use of Color
sources.finding: Meaning must not depend only on hue: accompany with labels, shapes, text, focus indicators.

neutral paper backgrounds; no color-only retrieval cue
future pref controlled theme; no impact on scoring

new_key_risk: L2 text enhancement can improve form noticing but harm meaning processing: Lee & Huang d=+0.22 grammar vs d=-0.26 meaning. Meaning-first required.
